_note: FASB ASC Topic 944 — Financial Services: Insurance. Each sub-topic follows the four-section schema: chapter_content / need / evolution / gaap_comparison.
manual: FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 944 — Financial Services: Insurance

standards.title: Overall — Scope and Objectives
standards.summary: Scope, objectives, and overall organization of ASC 944.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-10 establishes the scope of the topic — applicable to entities that issue insurance contracts, including life, P&C, health, financial-guaranty, mortgage-guaranty, and title insurance. It also covers reinsurance contracts. Excluded: warranty contracts (covered by ASC 460), service contracts not having insurance characteristics, and self-insurance.
standards.need: Defines what falls under insurance accounting versus other revenue/contract accounting standards. Without a clear scope, multi-line entities (e.g., a manufacturer offering extended warranties) would face ambiguity.

evolution.change: Original codification of legacy FAS 60, FAS 97, FAS 113, FAS 120, FAS 91, etc. into Topic 944.
ASU 2018-12 (LDTI) introduced significant updates to long-duration sub-topics 30 and 40.

gaap_comparison.stat: NAIC AP&P Manual — broader, covers entire entity

standards.title: Insurance Activities (Reinsurance)
standards.summary: Reinsurance accounting — the canonical risk-transfer test in 944-20-15-41 and prospective vs retrospective bifurcation.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-20 covers all reinsurance accounting. Section 15-41 sets the risk-transfer test: a contract receives reinsurance accounting only if the reinsurer assumes significant insurance risk with reasonable possibility of significant loss. Failed risk transfer triggers deposit accounting. Prospective contracts (covering future events) recognize ceded premium over the coverage period. Retrospective contracts (covering prior events) defer any gain through the interest method.
standards.need: Prevents financial-engineering 'reinsurance' that synthetically inflates earnings or surplus without real risk transfer.

evolution.change: Risk-transfer interpretation refined post-AIG/Gen Re finite-reinsurance scandal.
SEC comment letters increasingly challenge multi-year aggregate covers.

gaap_comparison.gaap: ASC 944-20-15-41 — significant insurance risk + reasonable possibility of loss

standards.title: Presentation of Financial Statements
standards.summary: Insurance-specific income-statement and balance-sheet presentation requirements.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-205 establishes the presentation of insurance-entity financial statements — separate captions for premium revenue, benefits & claims, DAC amortization, and reinsurance impacts.
standards.need: Provides users with comparable, standardized financial-statement presentation across insurance entities.

standards.title: Balance Sheet
standards.summary: Insurance balance-sheet classification and presentation.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-210 specifies balance-sheet classification — separate accounts, policyholder reserves, DAC, reinsurance recoverables, and insurance-related receivables.
standards.need: Standardized line-item presentation.

standards.title: Income Statement
standards.summary: Insurance-specific income-statement classification.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-225 specifies income-statement classification — premium revenue, benefits, DAC amortization, investment income, and reinsurance impacts.
standards.need: Standardized income-statement format for insurance entities.

standards.title: Notes to Financial Statements
standards.summary: Insurance-specific note disclosures.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-235 mandates insurance-specific note disclosures — reserve rollforwards, reinsurance disclosure, MRB rollforward, and DAC rollforward.
standards.need: Provides users with the granular disclosure needed to evaluate insurer performance and risk.

standards.title: Accounting Changes and Error Corrections
standards.summary: Accounting-change and error-correction guidance specific to insurance.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-250 provides insurance-specific guidance on accounting changes (e.g., LDTI transition) and error corrections.
standards.need: Coordinates broad ASC 250 with insurance-specific transition mechanics.

standards.title: Changing Prices
standards.summary: Inflation-adjusted disclosure (largely historical).
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-255 covers historical changing-price disclosures (largely retired).
standards.need: Historical guidance retained for legacy reporting.

standards.title: Risks and Uncertainties
standards.summary: Risk-and-uncertainty disclosures for insurers.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-275 mandates disclosure of significant risks and uncertainties including catastrophe exposure, concentration of insured risks, and reserve estimation uncertainty.
standards.need: Provides users with insight into the inherent uncertainty in insurance financial statements.

standards.title: Acquisition Costs (DAC)
standards.summary: Capitalization and amortization of incremental, direct contract-acquisition costs. Post-LDTI: constant-level amortization replaces EGP unlocking.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-30 defines DAC as the incremental, direct costs of acquiring an insurance contract — first-year commissions exceeding renewal rates, underwriting expenses traceable to issued contracts, and direct contract-issuance costs. Marketing and overhead are excluded. Post-ASU 2018-12 (LDTI), DAC amortizes on a constant-level basis tied to a denominator (e.g., inforce face, policy count). No interest accrual; annual review of denominator assumption is prospective only.
standards.need: Matches acquisition costs against the revenue stream they generate, providing a more representative income statement than expensing all costs at issuance.

evolution.change: ASU 2010-26 narrowed capitalizable costs to incremental and direct.
ASU 2018-12 (LDTI) replaced EGP-based amortization with constant-level.

standards.title: Receivables (Reinsurance)
standards.summary: Recoverables from reinsurers; CECL allowance under ASC 326-20.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-310 governs reinsurance recoverables on paid and unpaid losses. Recoverables are presented as separate assets on the balance sheet (never netted against gross liabilities) and carry a CECL allowance per ASC 326-20. Concentration disclosures are required when one reinsurer represents a material portion of total recoverables.
standards.need: Maintains the indemnity-contract principle (cedent remains primarily liable) while recognizing credit deterioration on long-dated recoverables.

evolution.change: ASU 2016-13 (CECL) added the lifetime expected-credit-loss allowance.

gaap_comparison.stat: Schedule F authorized vs unauthorized non-admission

standards.title: Other Assets and Deferred Costs
standards.summary: Catch-all guidance for assets and deferred costs not addressed in other 944 sub-topics, including VOBA from business combinations.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-340 provides accounting for other assets and deferred costs unique to insurance, most notably Value of Business Acquired (VOBA) — the present value of future profits embedded in acquired insurance contracts. VOBA is amortized on a basis consistent with the acquired contract's DAC method (constant-level under LDTI).
standards.need: Captures the economic value of an in-force insurance book at acquisition without leaving the acquirer's balance sheet asymmetric.

evolution.change: VOBA amortization aligned with LDTI constant-level approach.

gaap_comparison.gaap: Recognized at fair value; amortized constant-level
gaap_comparison.stat: Effectively N/A — replaced by goodwill admission limits

standards.title: Claim Costs and Liabilities for Future Policy Benefits
standards.summary: Combines short-duration unpaid claims, long-duration LFPB (LDTI-revised), and MRBs. The single largest sub-topic for insurers.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-40 spans three measurement worlds: (1) short-duration unpaid claims & LAE measured at best estimate, undiscounted; (2) long-duration LFPB measured at the cohort level under LDTI with annual unlocking and current upper-medium-grade discount; (3) market risk benefits (MRBs) at fair value with non-performance risk in OCI. The 30-19A paragraph specifically defines MRBs.
standards.need: Provides the principal liability framework for insurance contracts. Reserves accuracy is the cornerstone of insurer earnings quality and regulatory solvency.

evolution.change: ASU 2015-09 added short-duration loss-development triangle disclosure.
Long-term care portfolios across the industry triggered $200M-$2B unlockings.

gaap_comparison.delta: Both principle-based; differ in unlocking rules

gaap_comparison.gaap: Fair value; OCI for own credit

standards.title: Liabilities — Other (Universal Life)
standards.summary: Account-balance liability for universal life and deferred annuities; post-LDTI alignment with deposit-style accounting.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-405 addresses other long-duration liabilities, principally the policyholder account balance for universal life and deferred annuity contracts. Balance equals deposits plus interest credited less withdrawals, COI charges, and expense loads. Front-end loads create an unearned-revenue liability amortized alongside DAC.
standards.need: Accurate reflection of insurer obligations to policyholders under deposit-style contracts.

standards.title: Commitments
standards.summary: Insurance-specific commitments and contingencies.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-440 covers insurance-specific commitments — investment commitments, reinsurance commitments, and lease commitments specific to insurance operations.
standards.need: Captures off-balance-sheet commitments material to solvency.

standards.title: Debt
standards.summary: Insurance-entity debt classification and presentation.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-470 covers debt issued by insurance entities — long-term debt, surplus notes (where applicable), and trust-preferred securities.
standards.need: Standardizes debt presentation across insurance issuers.

standards.title: Policyholder Dividends
standards.summary: Liability accrual for participating-policy dividends.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-50 requires liability accrual for policyholder dividends as the entity becomes obligated. For mutual-life insurers, annual dividend declarations from divisible surplus drive the year-end accrual. Stock companies issuing participating contracts apply the same model.
standards.need: Matches dividend expense to the period in which the obligation arises — typically over the policy year on participating contracts.

evolution.change: Aligned with LDTI cohort granularity for participating-contract dividends.

standards.title: Equity
standards.summary: Insurance-entity equity classification and dividend mechanics.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-505 covers equity classification and dividend mechanics specific to insurance entities — dividend restrictions, retained earnings analysis, and AOCI components.
standards.need: Captures the regulatory dividend restrictions applicable to insurance entities.

gaap_comparison.delta: GAAP equity vs STAT surplus differ materially

standards.title: Premium Deficiency and Loss Recognition
standards.summary: Trigger for recognizing additional reserve when expected costs exceed unearned premium plus DAC plus expected investment income.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-60-25 establishes the premium deficiency reserve trigger: when the present value of expected future losses, LAE, and maintenance costs exceeds unearned premium reserve plus DAC plus expected investment income, recognize the shortfall. Aggregation level is consistent with how the entity manages and measures profitability — typically line of business.
standards.need: Loss-recognition mechanism that prevents the balance sheet from showing a profitable book that is in fact economically deficient.

standards.title: Revenue Recognition (Premium)
standards.summary: Premium recognition rules — short-duration ratably; long-duration when due; deposit contracts no premium revenue.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-605 specifies premium revenue recognition (insurance contracts are excluded from ASC 606). Short-duration policies earn premium pro-rata over the coverage period. Long-duration policies recognize revenue when due. Deposit contracts (UL, deferred annuities) have no premium revenue — premium is recorded as a deposit and revenue comes from charges.
standards.need: Provides line-by-line revenue recognition consistent with the economics of each contract type.

evolution.change: ASC 606 explicitly excluded insurance contracts; ASC 944-605 retained for them.

standards.title: Other Expenses
standards.summary: Insurance-specific expense categories including premium taxes, guaranty-fund assessments, and policyholder dividends payable.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-720 addresses expense categories unique to insurance — premium taxes, guaranty-fund assessments (recognized when probable and estimable), and policyholder dividends payable. Premium taxes accrue as premium is earned.
standards.need: Provides consistent treatment for insurer-specific expense categories that don't fit cleanly into other expense topics.

standards.title: Income Taxes
standards.summary: Insurance-specific income-tax considerations.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-740 covers insurance-specific income-tax matters including IRC §846 loss-reserve discounting, IRC §848 DAC tax-amortization, and FBE/non-FBE life-insurance company classification.
standards.need: Captures the unique tax-accounting issues facing insurance entities.

gaap_comparison.delta: Both leverage federal tax basis with admission overlay

standards.title: Separate Accounts
standards.summary: Presentation and measurement of separate-account assets and liabilities for variable annuities, variable life, and pension separate accounts.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-80 requires separate-account assets and corresponding policyholder liabilities to be presented in summary form on the balance sheet at fair value. Investment performance flows directly to policyholders. The general account retains contingent obligations under guaranteed minimum benefit provisions, accounted for under MRB rules (post-LDTI).
standards.need: Reflects the contractual structure where policyholders bear investment risk on segregated assets.

evolution.change: MRB framework introduced for general-account guarantees.

standards.title: Business Combinations
standards.summary: Business combinations involving insurance entities — VOBA recognition.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-805 governs business combinations involving insurance entities, with the unique requirement to recognize VOBA at fair value.
standards.need: Addresses the asymmetry that would otherwise occur when an acquirer takes on insurance liabilities at fair value but no offsetting asset.

gaap_comparison.delta: GAAP recognizes VOBA; STAT does not

standards.title: Derivatives and Hedging
standards.summary: Insurance-specific derivative and hedging considerations.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-815 cross-references ASC 815 with insurance-specific overlays — embedded derivatives in insurance hosts, MRB hedging, and replication transactions.
standards.need: Captures insurance-specific derivative use cases distinct from general financial-instrument framework.

standards.title: Fair Value Measurement
standards.summary: Insurance-specific fair-value-measurement considerations.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-820 cross-references ASC 820 with insurance-specific overlays for Level 3 valuations and unique insurance-contract fair values.
standards.need: Captures the fair-value-measurement challenges unique to insurance — MRBs, illiquid insurance receivables, and Level 3 investment portfolios.

standards.title: Financial Instruments — Insurance
standards.summary: Cross-references to ASC 825 for fair-value option and ASC 815 for embedded derivatives, with insurance-specific overlays for MRB classification.
standards.chapter_content: ASC 944-825 connects insurance accounting to the broader financial-instrument framework. Embedded derivatives in insurance host contracts are bifurcated under ASC 815-15. The fair-value option (ASC 825-10-25) is available for certain financial instruments including some long-duration contracts. Post-LDTI, MRBs replace embedded derivative bifurcation for most variable-annuity guarantees.
standards.need: Avoids redundancy by leveraging the general financial-instrument framework while accommodating insurance-specific structures.

evolution.change: MRB designation introduced under LDTI for variable-annuity guarantees.

gaap_comparison.gaap: Fair value with OCI for own credit
